_readme: Neighborhood guide content. Edit the words here, then the guide pages rebuild themselves (GitHub runs scripts/update-neighborhoods.mjs). Numbers (Census and homes for sale) are filled in automatically; do not type them here. To give a town a video or photo, put the file in media/towns/ and set media.video / media.poster / media.photo to its path. Bill's tall drone clips go in media.clips (video, poster, title) and show in a 'from the air' section. Fair housing: describe places, homes and amenities, never the people who live there or who a place is 'good for'.
schoolGradesNote: Mississippi Department of Education 2025-26 district accountability grades, released October 2026. Grades are for the district as a whole; individual schools can differ. Attendance zones change, so confirm the school for any address with the district.

towns.name: Gulfport
towns.tagline: The Coast's largest city, built around a working port and a long stretch of beach.
intro: Gulfport is the largest city on the Mississippi Gulf Coast and shares the job of Harrison County seat with Biloxi. It was founded at the end of the 1800s as a railroad and shipping town, and the Port of Gulfport is still a big part of the local economy.

Homes range from older cottages and bungalows near downtown and the beach to newer subdivisions north of Interstate 10. The city covers a lot of ground, so it is worth narrowing a search by ZIP code and commute.

highlights.name: Jones Park and the Gulfport harbor
highlights.text: Waterfront park, marina and event space where US 90 meets US 49.

highlights.name: Mississippi Aquarium
highlights.text: Downtown aquarium with indoor and outdoor exhibits, opened in 2020.

highlights.name: Ship Island excursions
highlights.text: Seasonal ferry from the Gulfport harbor to West Ship Island in Gulf Islands National Seashore.

highlights.name: Downtown Gulfport
highlights.text: Restaurants, bars and shops a few blocks from the beach.

highlights.name: Gulfport-Biloxi International Airport
highlights.text: The Coast's main commercial airport, inside Gulfport city limits.

highlights.name: Gulfport Premium Outlets
highlights.text: Outlet shopping at Interstate 10 and US 49.

towns.gettingAround: US 90 runs along the beach, Interstate 10 crosses the north side of the city, and US 49 heads north toward Hattiesburg. The Naval Construction Battalion Center (the Seabee base) is in Gulfport, and Keesler Air Force Base in Biloxi is a short drive east.

schools.district: Harrison County School District (some areas, mostly north)

towns.name: Biloxi
towns.tagline: French colonial roots, a seafood heritage, and the Coast's casino and entertainment hub.
intro: Biloxi sits on a peninsula between the Mississippi Sound and the Back Bay of Biloxi. It has French colonial roots and a long history as a seafood and shipbuilding town, and today it is also home to Keesler Air Force Base and most of the Coast's large casino resorts.

Housing runs from historic homes in east Biloxi to newer neighborhoods north of the Back Bay in the Woolmarket area. Being close to the water is part of daily life here, so flood zones and insurance are worth checking early.

highlights.name: Biloxi Lighthouse
highlights.text: Cast-iron lighthouse from 1848, standing in the median of US 90.

highlights.name: Ohr-O'Keefe Museum of Art
highlights.text: Museum campus designed by architect Frank Gehry, honoring potter George Ohr.

highlights.name: Maritime & Seafood Industry Museum
highlights.text: The story of Biloxi's fishing and boatbuilding history, at Point Cadet.

highlights.name: MGM Park
highlights.text: Minor league baseball stadium on the Back Bay side of downtown.

highlights.name: Mississippi Coast Coliseum
highlights.text: Concerts, shows and the convention center on the beach.

highlights.name: Biloxi Bay Bridge
highlights.text: US 90 bridge to Ocean Springs with a walking and biking path.

towns.gettingAround: US 90 follows the beach, Interstate 110 connects downtown to Interstate 10 across the Back Bay, and the Biloxi Bay Bridge leads east to Ocean Springs. Keesler Air Force Base is in the middle of the city.

towns.name: Long Beach
towns.tagline: A beach town between Gulfport and Pass Christian, with a harbor and a 500-year-old oak.
intro: Long Beach is a smaller city on the beach between Gulfport and Pass Christian. In the early 1900s it was known for radish farming; today it is mostly homes, a small-town downtown, and the Long Beach Harbor.
Streets south of the railroad sit close to the water under big live oaks, and neighborhoods north of the tracks run up toward Interstate 10.

highlights.name: Long Beach Harbor
highlights.text: Marina, boat launch and harbor front on US 90.

highlights.name: Friendship Oak
highlights.text: Live oak estimated at about 500 years old, on the University of Southern Mississippi Gulf Park campus.

highlights.name: USM Gulf Park
highlights.text: The University of Southern Mississippi's coastal campus.

highlights.name: The beach
highlights.text: A long sand beach with a walking path along US 90.

towns.gettingAround: US 90 runs along the beach, and Interstate 10 is a few miles north. Gulfport-Biloxi International Airport is a short drive east.

schools.note: Among the five highest point totals in the state in 2025-26.

towns.name: Pass Christian
towns.tagline: Historic homes on Scenic Drive, a working harbor, and the bridge to Bay St. Louis.
intro: Pass Christian sits at the western end of Harrison County, where the Bay of St. Louis meets the Mississippi Sound. It has been a summer destination since the 1800s, and Scenic Drive along the beach is lined with historic homes and live oaks.
The ZIP code also covers land outside city limits, including Henderson Point and areas to the north, so lot sizes and home styles vary a lot.

highlights.name: Scenic Drive
highlights.text: Historic homes facing the beach under a canopy of live oaks.

highlights.name: Pass Christian Harbor
highlights.text: Harbor with an oyster and shrimp fleet, a yacht club and waterfront restaurants.

highlights.name: Pass Christian Yacht Club
highlights.text: A sailing club with roots in the 1800s.

highlights.name: Downtown Pass Christian
highlights.text: A small downtown of shops and restaurants near the harbor.

towns.gettingAround: US 90 runs along the beach and crosses the Bay St. Louis Bridge to Hancock County. Interstate 10 is reached by Menge Avenue and other roads to the north.

towns.name: Bay St. Louis
towns.tagline: Old Town shops and galleries on a bluff over the water, and the Hancock County seat.
intro: Bay St. Louis is the seat of Hancock County, on the west side of the Bay of St. Louis. Old Town, its walkable downtown on a bluff above the beach, is known for galleries, restaurants and a monthly art walk.
Homes range from cottages in Old Town to larger lots and newer houses out toward Interstate 10. NASA's Stennis Space Center is in Hancock County, north of town.

highlights.name: Old Town Bay St. Louis
highlights.text: Shops, galleries and restaurants above the beach, with a Second Saturday art walk.

highlights.name: Bay St. Louis Municipal Harbor
highlights.text: Marina and boardwalk at the foot of Old Town.

highlights.name: Historic L&N train depot
highlights.text: Restored depot that houses the Alice Moseley Folk Art and Antique Museum and a Mardi Gras museum.

highlights.name: Stennis Space Center
highlights.text: NASA's rocket engine test center, with the INFINITY Science Center visitor center at I-10.

highlights.name: Bay St. Louis Bridge
highlights.text: US 90 bridge to Pass Christian with a walking path.

towns.gettingAround: US 90 crosses the Bay St. Louis Bridge east to Harrison County and runs west to Waveland. Interstate 10 is north of town, and New Orleans is about an hour west.

schools.note: Highest point total of Mississippi's 148 districts in 2025-26.

clips.title: Bay St. Louis Harbor and the bridge

towns.name: Ocean Springs
towns.tagline: A walkable, art-filled downtown across the bay from Biloxi.
intro: Ocean Springs is across Biloxi Bay from Biloxi, in Jackson County. The French built Fort Maurepas here in 1699, one of the first European settlements on the Gulf Coast. Today the downtown along Washington Avenue and Government Street is known for restaurants, shops and the arts.
Neighborhoods range from older streets near downtown and Front Beach to newer subdivisions toward Interstate 10 and the Gulf Park Estates area.

highlights.name: Downtown Ocean Springs
highlights.text: Restaurants, shops and live music along Washington Avenue and Government Street.

highlights.name: Walter Anderson Museum of Art
highlights.text: Museum dedicated to the Ocean Springs artist Walter Anderson.

highlights.name: Peter Anderson Arts & Crafts Festival
highlights.text: Large outdoor arts festival held downtown each November.

highlights.name: Gulf Islands National Seashore, Davis Bayou
highlights.text: National park area with trails, a visitor center and a boat launch.

highlights.name: Front Beach
highlights.text: Beach and harbor along Biloxi Bay.

towns.gettingAround: US 90 crosses the Biloxi Bay Bridge west to Biloxi, Interstate 10 runs north of town, and Keesler Air Force Base and the Ingalls shipyard in Pascagoula are both a short drive.

schools.note: Among the five highest point totals in the state in 2025-26.

towns.name: D'Iberville
towns.tagline: On the Back Bay of Biloxi, where Interstate 10 meets Interstate 110.
intro: D'Iberville sits on the north shore of the Back Bay of Biloxi and is named for the French explorer Pierre Le Moyne d'Iberville. It became a city in 1988 and has grown quickly around the Interstate 10 and Interstate 110 interchange.
Much of the housing is newer, with subdivisions north of the interstate and older homes along the bay. Shopping, restaurants and quick access to Biloxi make it a central spot on the Coast.

highlights.name: The Promenade
highlights.text: Large open-air shopping center at Interstate 10.

highlights.name: Back Bay of Biloxi
highlights.text: Waterfront, boat launches and fishing along the bay.

highlights.name: Scarlet Pearl Casino Resort
highlights.text: Casino resort with a golf course, on the Back Bay.

towns.gettingAround: Interstate 10 and Interstate 110 meet here, and I-110 crosses the Back Bay straight into downtown Biloxi and the beach. Keesler Air Force Base is a few minutes south.
